headline: Yields hit 19-year highs, but AI-name bullishness holds up
body: Treasury yields are doing most of the talking this week: the 10-year climbed as high as roughly 5.25-5.27%, its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year pushed above 5.5%. That move pressured equities into Monday's close, with the Dow off 0.7%, the S&P 500 down 0.8%, and the Nasdaq slipping almost 1%. The yield spike is tangled up with an escalating US-Iran standoff that has kept oil elevated and reinforced bets on further Fed tightening, with a parade of Fed speakers on today's calendar and Wednesday's PCE print and Friday's jobs report still to come. Futures were mixed into Tuesday's open, with Nasdaq-100 contracts edging higher even as Dow and S&P futures wobbled, and the S&P 500 remains only about 1.4% below its August record - a sign the selloff has hit sentiment harder than actual positioning so far.

Underneath the rate story, the AI trade continues to swing between extremes rather than settle into a clear trend, with chip and hyperscaler names whipsawing on infrastructure-spending headlines. Retail chatter tracked from Reddit's WallStreetBets still skews toward the same handful of AI megacaps - Nvidia, Alphabet, and Meta - showing up as the most-discussed names with a generally bullish lean, even as the macro backdrop turns more cautious on rates and oil. That gap, rising anxiety in the bond market against persistent enthusiasm for AI infrastructure names, looks like the more interesting tension in today's tape than any single index move; the retail read here leans more on a narrow set of trending megacap tickers than on broad, market-wide conviction.
